neighbours.label: 'can' + an effect or role verb after a generic cause as subject: 'X can cause / can lead to / can act as / can serve as …' (peaks on can, cause, act, as); a person's ability ('children can swim') stays quiet
fire: Too much salt in the diet can cause high blood pressure over time.
Lack of sleep and constant stress can lead to memory problems in adults.
A thick layer of mulch can act as insulation for the roots in winter.
Loose wiring and damp walls can both cause fires in older houses.
An empty jam jar can serve as a simple vase for wild flowers.
Prolonged drought and overgrazing can lead to severe erosion of the soil.
Cracked tiles and blocked gutters can cause leaks during heavy rain.
A row of tall hedges can act as a windbreak for the vegetable beds.
quiet: Too much salt was found in the diet of patients with high blood pressure.
Adults with memory problems often report a lack of sleep and constant stress.
My sister can juggle five oranges and ride a unicycle at once.
The fire in the older house started near loose wiring and a damp wall.
You can pick wild flowers along the path and put them in a jar.
The soil was badly eroded after a prolonged drought and years of overgrazing.
The roofer can come on Thursday to look at the cracked tiles.
Our neighbour can speak four languages and play the cello.
